32 KiB page (4 packed streams, head width pow2-padded 1280 -> 2048, bf16
pinned) must reserve cdiv(min(window-1+max_in_flight_tokens, mml), 4)+1
blocks per request, and max_in_flight_tokens = 2 async batches x 16,384
batched tokens = 32,768. The conv page also sets the uniform page size,
scaling attention block_size to 32 (bf16) / 64 (fp8).

Capacity gain vs serving settings (same memory, vLLM's own math):

| max_model_len | batched tokens | bf16 pool | fp8 pool | gain |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8,192 | 16,384 | 317,012 | 335,644 | +5.9% |
| 131,072 | 16,384 | 1,200,271 | 1,303,934 | +8.6% |
| 131,072 | 8,192 | 2,239,900 | 2,509,704 | +12.0% |
| 131,072 | 2,048 | 6,392,807 | 8,189,269 | +28.1% |
| 524,288 | 16,384 | 3,967,258 | 4,681,299 | +18.0% |
| 1,048,576 | 16,384 | 6,442,622 | 8,237,213 | +27.9% |
| 1,048,576 | 8,192 | 9,356,357 | 13,272,591 | +41.9% |
| 1,048,576 | 2,048 | 14,159,015 | 24,509,531 | +73.1% |

fp8 KV halves attention KV bytes (7,168 -> 3,584
bytes/token/rank at TP4; the marginal per-token cost, carried by the 7 full-attention layers, with sliding-window layers capped at their 512-token window); the realized pool
gain depends on how much of the pool the model's conv-state admission
reserve consumes, which is orthogonal to this change.

### Pre-registered gate scorecard

Every acceptance threshold in EVAL_PLAN.md (the pre-registered plan
ships in the artifact archive), plus the tier-level deliverables that
changed, with verdicts and deviations declared. The plan's Tier 3 KL
metric was superseded by the per-position dNLL/top-1 design; the Tier
6 and Tier 7 deliverables are covered in their sections above:

| gate (as pre-registered) | verdict |
|---|---|
| Teacher-forced PPL delta <= 1.0% (wikitext-103, long-doc) | PASS, certified by Tier 3 v3 (noise-free pure-dtype design, production path, both fp8 configs): every stable-document bucket within +/-0.71%, deepest bucket ~0.1%. Declared deviations: PG19 book-length documents substituted for wikitext-103 (test split too short for 128K contexts); replication-unstable documents excluded from certification as demonstrated chaotic amplifiers (their swings are config-unstable and dtype-independent). |
| Top-1 agreement >= 99% (short) / >= 97% (long) | FAILED as written: observed 87.2-89.6%. The gate was ill-posed: the bf16-vs-bf16 control arm itself scores 88.2-90.5% under single-prefix perturbation, so no dtype could pass it. Reframed: fp8 top-1 agreement is within ~1pp of the same-server control in every bucket. |
| KV clip rate 0% observed at unity scale | FAILED on V: pooled 2.2e-5, worst pool 1.3e-4 (K: exact 0). The plan's own fallback (calibrated v_scale) was executed and reported; the failure is the mechanism behind the MATH-500 deficit. |
| GSM8K delta <= 1pt vs canonical evaluator | The canonical-evaluator cross-check was not run: serving is raw completions without chat template or reasoning mode, which is also why absolute GSM8K (82-85%) sits ~12pt below the model family's published baseline. Within-harness deltas: 0.83pt sheared (inside gate), 1.82pt score-mod (outside gate, fp8-favored, p=0.093). |
| RULER per-length recovery vs bf16 >= 97% (8K-64K) | NOT RUN; substituted by a custom paired single-needle NIAH (120/120 both dtypes). Declared limitation: no multi-needle, variable-tracking, or aggregation coverage. |
| Decode ITL regression at short context: none outside noise | PASS: decode-workload median TPOT 8.89 ms (bf16) vs 8.86 ms (fp8), single run per cell (Tier 6). |
| Tool-calling replay, 500 calls via gateway harness | RUN as pre-registered (see Tier 4): parity (475 vs 474 primary pass, McNemar p=1.0), 100% schema validity both arms, zero repairs. |
| Scale sweep {0.5, 1.0, 2.0} serving robustness | NOT RUN at serving level. Kernel tests sweep scales (0.5, 0.5, 1.5) and unity; serving-level scale evidence comes from the unity vs v_scale=3.0 A/B instead. |
| Optional e5m2 smoke test (storage dtype accepted, tests pass) | Deviation: the plan anticipated accepting e5m2 storage; the implementation rejects fp8_e5m2 with a clear error (e4m3 only), and the rejection gate tests pass (kernel + CPU). |
| minerva_math500 + run-level statistics | Not pre-registered; added exploratorily after GSM8K parity, then replicated (3 runs/arm) with the unity-scale V-clipping mechanism validated by the calibration A/B. Reported with run-level statistics. |

### Environment

vLLM v0.28.0, torch 2.13.0, triton 3.7.1, CUDA-capability SM100
(B200 183GB). Model: Inkling-Small 276B/12B MoE, nvfp4 checkpoint,
42 layers (35 sliding-window 512 + 7 global), 8 KV heads, head_dim 128,
sconv kernel 4, hybrid attention with learned relative position bias,
no RoPE.

</details>

items.title: [RFC]: fp8 KV cache support for Inkling on SM100-family GPUs
items.body:
### Motivation.

Inkling and Inkling-Small serve with a bf16 KV cache only. `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` fails at JIT warmup: the cache is allocated as uint8, nothing in the Inkling stack reinterprets it as an fp8 dtype, and both kernel backends assert on the dtype.

KV memory is the binding constraint for long context on memory-limited deployments. fp8 halves attention KV bytes across the stack (7,168 to 3,584 bytes/token/rank at TP4: the 7 full-attention layers at 1,024 bytes/token/layer; the 35 sliding-window layers hold only their 512-token window, so they do not scale with context). The realized pool gain depends on serving settings, because the per-request pool charge is dominated by the bf16-pinned conv-state admission reserve, which this change cannot touch. Measured through vLLM's own `get_kv_cache_configs` at the same memory budget:

| max_model_len | max_num_batched_tokens | pool gain (fp8 vs bf16) |
|---|---|---|
| 8,192 | 16,384 | +5.9% |
| 131,072 | 16,384 (serve default) | +8.6% |
| 131,072 | 2,048 | +28.1% |
| 1,048,576 | 16,384 | +27.9% |
| 1,048,576 | 2,048 | +73.1% |

The 1M configuration was validated live, not just modeled: two servers booted at max_model_len 1,048,576 measured +73.06% pool capacity against the +73.1% prediction, with capacity for 24 concurrent 1M-token requests under fp8 vs 14 under bf16 (vLLM's logged maximum concurrency), and cold-prefill TTFT at 0.84x bf16 at 1M. Kernel-level attention speedups reach 1.45x and grow with KV length.

### Proposed Change.

Two PRs, sequenced. The kernel PR merges first; the wiring PR references it; a follow-up bumps the vendored pin.

1. tml-fa4 kernel PR (vllm-project/tml-fa4#4): plain per-tensor fp8 e4m3 Q/KV support in the Blackwell sheared-bias forward kernel. 4 files, +148/-27, based on current main (b206834, the exact commit vLLM vendors). It adapts closed PR vllm-project/tml-fa4#1 and fixes a correctness bug in it: with fp8 P pre-scaled by 2\*\*8, the lazy-rescale slack that guarantees zero P clipping is log2(448) - 8 = 0.807, but that PR set rescale_threshold=4.0. Attention bias makes sub-threshold row-max jumps routine, clipping P (six deterministic test failures, 0.3-0.7 abs error, root cause proven by zero-bias diagnostic and three-arm bisection: threshold=0 fixes, max_offset=0 fixes, ex2-tuning-off does not). We ship rescale_threshold=0.75, chosen to guarantee the invariant with margin for compiler reassociation. The empirical failure onset sits between 1.5 and 2.0 with monotonic dose-response beyond it.

2. vLLM wiring PR: `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` for Inkling. 8 files, +596/-35 across two commits (the feature, plus a clean NotImplementedError for quantized KV dtypes on the ROCm path; non-test delta ~260 lines). Runtime-validated on v0.28.0; cherry-picks cleanly onto main as of 2026-08-28 (4c6c9d5).

3. Follow-up after (1) merges: bump the tml-fa4 GIT_TAG in cmake/external_projects/tml_fa4.cmake.

Design summary:

- Quant-on-store. K/V are already computed in fp32 inside the fused qkvr_prep store kernels; with fp8 active they are multiplied by the reciprocal scale, clamped to the e4m3 finite range (+/-448), and stored as e4m3. Write-path cost is -1.3% to +2.0% vs the bf16 store (median ratio 1.01); the added multiply+clamp+convert is offset by halved write bytes.
- Scales. Per-tensor, per-layer k_scale/v_scale, default 1.0, loaded from checkpoint tensors `model.llm.layers.<i>.attn.{k,v}_scale` through the standard loader path with no flags. Q is quantized with a static per-tensor scale after qkvr_prep.
- Kernel read path. The shipped sheared kernel takes fp8 Q/KV directly and adds no descale parameters; both descales are per-tensor scalars applied at the vLLM wrapper (fa4_rel_attention.py). The QK descale is folded into softmax_scale, so scores are descaled before the relative position bias is added and the bias term stays exact; the V descale is applied as a post-hoc multiply on the kernel output, which is linear in V. The fold sits outside the backend branch and is path-independent: the CuTe score-mod fallback receives the same folded softmax_scale and output multiply, since neither vendored varlen entry exposes descale parameters.
- Gating. SM100-family e4m3 only; a clear error is raised elsewhere. ROCm gains no fp8 path: quantized KV dtypes are rejected at layer construction (second wiring commit); non-quantized dtypes are untouched.
- Conv state stays bf16. It is pinned to model dtype, unaffected by kv_cache_dtype; conv-cache stores are untouched and verified bit-identical to the bf16 run.
- Load-time warning. If fp8 KV is enabled and the checkpoint carries v_scale tensors for fewer layers than run quantized (coverage-checked at model level from the loader's return value, since unity values are legitimate in a calibrated checkpoint), a warning names the measured failure mode; loaded scales are validated finite and positive.
- CI. New tests live under tests/models/inkling/ and are picked up by the existing B200 Inkling Buildkite entry (key inkling-unit-tests-b200); no CI config change.

### Evidence Summary

Serving measurements on B200 (SM100), vLLM v0.28.0, TP4, two identical 4-GPU servers (bf16 vs fp8), greedy, paired prompts. Kernel-level numbers are from a separate single-B200 host. The full evidence document with per-run artifacts and the pre-registered gate scorecard will be attached to the wiring PR.

| axis | result |
|---|---|
| kernel correctness | 160/160 tests across the three test files this change touches: both backends, fp8 x {sheared, scoremod} x scale sets x rel extents, atol/rtol 0.15 vs a dequantized-input fp32 reference, plus spec/warmup/gate tests |
| kernel latency | fp8 faster in 18/20 cases; best 1.45x (batched decode, kv=64K, b=32); worst regression +2.6% |
| long-context logprobs (book-length docs, longest 121K scored tokens, noise-free paired design, production path) | on the stable documents (5/10; the replication-unstable documents, four high-PPL and one at PPL 14, are excluded from certification because they amplify replication noise, see evidence doc), every position bucket within +/-0.71% PPL on both fp8 configs; deepest bucket (64K-128K) ~0.1%; median across all 10 docs +0.21% (unity) / +0.16% (calibrated); top-1 agreement rises with depth; no error compounding |
| GSM8K / MMLU (n=14,042) / IFEval / HumanEval | parity on all four on the score-mod path, paired McNemar per sample; GSM8K and MMLU repeated at parity on the production sheared path |
| tool calling, 500-call replay | 475 vs 474 pass, McNemar p=1.0; 100% JSON- and schema-valid on both arms; 50/50 negatives correctly silent |
| needle-in-a-haystack (custom paired single-needle test, substituted for the pre-registered RULER suite; no multi-needle or aggregation coverage) | 120/120 both dtypes to 120K; at the 1M boot, 27/27 paired retrievals including needles ~950K tokens behind the query |
| capacity, live 1M boot | +73.06% measured vs +73.1% predicted; 24 vs 14 concurrent 1M-token requests |
| TTFT, cold single request | 0.96x at 256K, 0.91x at 512K, 0.84x at 1M (fp8 faster, monotonic in context) |
| serving throughput | parity within +/-1.1% up to 32K contexts; +2.2% total tok/s and -2.3% TTFT at 100K prefill; two exceptions: decode-workload median TTFT +10.2% (143.7 to 158.3 ms, p99 improves) and mid-workload median TTFT +2.7% |

Known limitation: MATH-500 regresses at unity scale.

- -4.2pt mean (41.9 to 37.7, triplicate runs per arm, run-level p 0.05-0.10; direction consistent across all 9 cross-run pairings). Every other task in the battery is at parity.
- Mechanism, measured: V outliers clip at unity scale, concentrated in the global attention layers (max |V| = 1,272 vs e4m3 max 448; the worst global layer clips ~1 in 1,100 V elements). K never clips anywhere. Global layers carry long-range information, consistent with the deficit surfacing only on long-derivation math.
- Remedy: calibrated v_scale recovers about half the deficit (37.7 to 39.7 mean; the best calibrated run, 41.0, comes within 0.8pt of the weakest bf16 run at 41.8, while the best unity run reaches only 39.4) at no cost elsewhere (GSM8K 83.55% on the calibrated server, center of the healthy band). Per-layer calibration of this checkpoint touches 14 of 42 layers, all v_scale, no k_scale.
- The wiring PR ships the coverage-checked warning. A standalone calibration utility exists: it hooks the fused store sites, measures real per-layer K/V ranges, derives clip-free per-layer scales, and writes them into the checkpoint for the existing loader. llm-compressor cannot calibrate this model because its HF-side observers never see Inkling's post-norm/post-conv fused store sites.

### Related Finding

The conv-state admission reserve that mutes the capacity gain at serve defaults is a separate, dtype-independent accounting behavior: tiny-window SlidingWindowSpec conv state is charged a per-request in-flight reserve that reaches 84% of per-request blocks. It affects any KV compression on hybrid conv models, not just this change. Filed separately as vllm-project/vllm#54703; it is referenced here to explain the sensitivity table above.

### Feedback Requested

1. Calibration tool placement. The documented KV-scale pathway is out-of-tree calibration via llm-compressor, which cannot observe this model's fused store sites (K is stored post-rms-norm and post-conv inside a fused kernel). Our prepared default: keep the utility out-of-tree and add a short Inkling section to docs/features/quantization/quantized_kvcache.md (drafted, ready to include). Alternatives if preferred: land it under examples/, or upstream the flow into llm-compressor as the long-term home.
2. Unity-scale serving behavior. Given the measured MATH-500 regression at unity scale, should serving an fp8 KV checkpoint without v_scale tensors warn (current behavior) or refuse unless explicitly opted in? The warning matches the existing unity-scale warning convention in BaseKVCacheMethod.process_weights_after_loading; we kept that precedent and would want a strong reason to diverge from it for one model.
3. ROCm scope. This proposal gates fp8 KV to SM100-family e4m3; the ROCm path rejects quantized KV dtypes at layer construction with an explicit NotImplementedError (included in the wiring PR, with a CPU test). A tracking issue for ROCm parity is drafted and ready to file if wanted.
4. Checkpoint scale schema. The emitted tensor names are in vLLM's canonical post-remap form and an opt-in flag records kv_cache_quant_algo=FP8 so kv_cache_dtype="auto" resolves to fp8 for downstream consumers. Any objection to that convention for this model?

### Feedback Period.

At least one week. Two weeks preferred: reproducing the end-to-end evidence requires B200 hardware.

### CC List.

Quantization: @mgoin @robertgshaw2-redhat @tlrmchlsmth @yewentao256 @pavanimajety @zyongye. Attention: @LucasWilkinson @MatthewBonanni. Inkling: @mikekg. @WoosukKwon authored vllm-project/tml-fa4#1, which the kernel PR adapts.

### Any Other Things.

- AI assistance disclosure: AI was used to implement, benchmark, debug, and document this work. The human submitter has reviewed every changed line and can explain and defend the implementation. Commits carry Co-authored-by trailers alongside Signed-off-by, per the contributing guide.
- Per the contributing guide's threshold, this RFC is optional (the wiring PR's non-test delta is ~260 lines); it is posted alongside the PRs (the wiring PR stays in draft) to collect design feedback, primarily on the questions above.
- Two pre-registered gates failed as written and are disclosed in the evidence document's scorecard. The top-1 agreement gate (>=99% short / >=97% long) was ill-posed: the bf16-vs-bf16 control arm itself scores 88.2-90.5% under prefix perturbation, and fp8 agreement is within ~1pt of that control in every bucket. The zero-KV-clip-at-unity gate failed on V (pooled 2.2e-5; K exact 0): this is the V-clipping mechanism behind the MATH-500 deficit described above. The scorecard also records that RULER was replaced by the custom paired single-needle NIAH noted in the evidence table, and the canonical-evaluator GSM8K cross-check was not run (its pre-registered bound is a <=1.0pt delta; within-harness deltas: 0.83pt on the sheared path, inside that bound; 1.82pt on the score-mod path, outside it, fp8-favored).

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Bug][Spec Decode]: DFlash is a net loss at long context (~185k) on hybrid GDN models - drafter re-scans full accumulated KV every cycle; no per-sequence-length disable hook
items.body:
### Summary

On hybrid GDN models (Qwen3.5-family), DFlash speculative decoding becomes a **net slowdown** at long context: single-stream 185k-context decode drops from ~71 tok/s (spec OFF) to ~16 tok/s (DT=4). At short context the same setup is a large win (218 tok/s at DT=8), so this is specifically a long-context failure mode - and there is currently no per-sequence-length hook to disable/attenuate speculation the way batch-size-based hooks exist.

### Measurements (RTX 4090 x4 TP4, vLLM 0.28.0, Qwen3.5-family hybrid GDN target + DFlash2 drafter, single stream)

| config | 185k decode | short-context decode |
|---|---|---|
| SPEC_OFF | ~71 tok/s | - |
| DFlash DT2 | 12.1 tok/s | - |
| DFlash DT4 | 16.0 tok/s | ~190 tok/s |
| DFlash DT8 | - | 218 tok/s |

DT scaling makes it *worse* at 185k (DT2 < DT4 < ...), which is the opposite of short context. CUDA graphs are not the cause (eager 14.7 vs graph 15.0 tok/s at 185k). Numbers are medians of repeated runs.

### Root cause (profiled)

The drafter builds its own KV cache by projecting target hidden states, and that cache **accumulates to the full context** (~185k). Every cycle:

- the drafter's 6 cross-attention layers each run FA over the entire accumulated drafter KV with only the small query block (1 + DT tokens),
- on top of the target's own full-attention layers.

At 185k this is ~182 ms of FA kernel time per cycle (GPU fully occupied), so verification wins from speculation are completely eaten by the drafter's full-context scan. The per-cycle KV *projection* is already incremental (only new tokens are projected via `precompute_and_store_context_kv`); the cost is the unavoidable full-context attention in the drafter itself.

### Why filing this

Related work targets other parts of this path:

- #43594 batches the per-layer KV *cache writes* (launch overhead, microseconds) - orthogonal to the ~182 ms/cycle attention cost.
- #52559 (graph-aware adaptive K) adapts draft length by batch/graph state - not by context length.
- #54690 blocks the draft-KV-fp8 experiment on SM89 (halving drafter KV bandwidth is one candidate mitigation we could not even measure).

But nothing today lets a deployment say "stop speculating beyond N context tokens".

### Suggested directions

1. **Cheap + general**: a per-sequence-length speculative control, e.g. extend `num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size`-style scheduling with a sequence-length dimension (`speculative_disable_by_seq_len` / `num_speculative_tokens_per_seq_len`), so long-context requests fall back to normal decode automatically. Today we have to run a separate server with spec disabled for long-context traffic.
2. **Drafter-side**: limit the drafter's cross-attention to a sliding window of recent context (acceptance-rate trade-off, likely needs training-time support - noted for completeness).
3. **Kernel-side**: draft KV in fp8 to halve the scan bandwidth - currently unreachable on Ada due to #54690.

Happy to provide full profile traces (torch profiler) and reproduce on demand.

items.title: [RFC]: Per-KV-cache-group prefix-cache retention, with a hit-min exemption for hit-inert EAGLE sliding-window draft groups
items.body:
### Motivation.

**Summary.** On hybrid models that carry an EAGLE-style sliding-window draft group (DFlash/DSpark-shaped drafters), that group hashes `cdiv(sliding_window - 1, block_size) + 1` block ids at *every* prefix-cache boundary and frees them *cached* onto the protected tail of the one LRU that all groups share, while — once it is exempted from the hit `min` — contributing nothing to the reconciled hit length. On a GLM-5.3-Flash deployment this one group spends 87% of the prefix cache and caps coexisting conversations at ~50K tokens each. A per-group retention interval, combined with exempting such hit-inert groups from the hit `min`, restored ~4× the coexisting-conversation capacity with the fine hit grid kept for the target model's groups, and a third party reproduced 99.95% cached across alternating 120K conversations. All numbers below are **deployment evidence from a vLLM fork**, not upstream verification; the code reading is against upstream `main` @ `22df3a3`. This RFC asks for agreement on the policy before any code is posted as a PR.

**Where the cost comes from (upstream `main` @ `22df3a3`, verified).**

- `--prefix-cache-retention-interval` (`vllm/config/cache.py:156-158`, `vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:530`) reaches the coordinator as one scalar, `KVCacheCoordinator.retention_interval` (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py:158`), and is handed unchanged to every manager at both `cache_blocks` sites (`:306-326` base, `:740-768` hybrid).
- Everything below the coordinator is already per group: `SingleTypeKVCacheManager.cache_blocks(..., retention_interval=None)` (`vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:432-436`), and each `reachable_block_mask` interprets it against its own block size and window (`:485-`, `:1010-`, `:1472-`).
- A sliding-window group needs `need = _contiguous_blocks_for_hit(window, block_size, use_eagle)` contiguous blocks at every retained boundary (`:898-908`, `:1028`); a full-attention group needs one block per boundary. Those SWA blocks are freed by `remove_skipped_blocks` -> `_remove_blocks_in_range` -> `BlockPool.free_blocks` (`:632`, `:605`), and because they are hashed they go to `blocks_to_evict_last` / `append_n`, the LRU *tail* (`vllm/v1/core/block_pool.py:723-747`). Full-attention blocks stay allocated until request end; Mamba align-mode state blocks may also be freed mid-request (`single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:1529-1557`), but a 3584-token Mamba group frees one id per segment where the draft group frees 33. The group with the least reusable state gets the most eviction protection.
- `HybridKVCacheCoordinator.find_longest_cache_hit` folds every attention group, EAGLE draft group included, into the reconciled hit (`kv_cache_coordinator.py:770-903`, `curr_hit_length = _new_hit_length` at `:871`). So giving the draft group a sparser retention on `main` today would shorten everyone's hit — which is why the fork below carries a `min` exemption first.

**Measured (deployment evidence: GLM-5.3-Flash, 2× DGX Spark, TP=2, DFlash2 draft k=7; vLLM fork `0.1.dev20051+g487ecf187`; GLM-5.3-Flash support upstream is #53906).** Groups: MLA block 3584, four Mamba "align" groups at 3584, one EAGLE sliding-window draft group with window 2048 / block 64, scheduler block 3584; one `BlockPool` of 643 block ids (642 usable; derived from the logged `max_concurrency`, see *Any Other Things*).

| group | block ids per cached 3584-token segment (dense retention) |
|---|---:|
| full attention (MLA) | 1 |
| Mamba × 4 | 4 |
| **draft sliding window** | **33** (`cdiv(2047, 64) + 1`) |
| total | 38 |

Two conversations of `S` segments coexist only while `642 >= 43·S` (each of B's segments pops 38 ids while A's cached draft tail contributes 33 back), i.e. `S <= 14.9`. Measured on a clean server: 14 segments OK / 17 evicting; pair ladders at 45K / 56K / 66K tokens hit 99% / 0% / 0%.

Raising the single global `--prefix-cache-retention-interval` to 14336 restored the ladder to 99 / 98 / 97 / 96% at 45K / 56K / 66K / 80K — but it bought that capacity by coarsening *everyone's* retention grid: a diverging sub-agent prefix then hit only 45% of a ~29K prompt instead of landing on the 3584 grid.

With per-group retention — retention `0` (reachable-boundary tails only) on the draft group, dense for MLA/Mamba — and the draft group exempted from the hit `min`, the per-segment cost drops to 5 ids (+33 per turn boundary), projected `S <= 54` (~195K tokens per conversation) with the 3584 hit grid kept. Independent reproduction by a third-party tester on a different 2× DGX Spark deployment (`max_model_len=524288`, `max_num_seqs=4`), two distinct 120K-token conversations alternated A -> B -> A -> B:

```
A cold             cached      0 / 119,995   TTFT 174.522s
A warm             cached 119,936 / 119,995   TTFT   0.581s
B cold             cached      0 / 119,995   TTFT 174.392s
B warm             cached 119,936 / 119,995   TTFT   0.590s
A return after B   cached 119,936 / 119,995   TTFT   0.567s
B return after A   cached 119,936 / 119,995   TTFT   0.567s
```

99.95% cached on every return, where the same shape previously evicted the parked conversation. Sources: https://github.com/MiaAI-Lab/GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3-2x-DGX-Sparks/pull/83 (per-group retention; the tester's receipt above is in its comments) and https://github.com/MiaAI-Lab/GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3-2x-DGX-Sparks/pull/84 (fine-grained hits, tested together). Those are recipe overlays on a fork; nothing there applies to `main` as-is.

### Proposed Change.

Three parts, in this order. The ask is agreement on 1 and 3 before any of the code is posted as a PR.

1. **Exempt hit-inert sliding-window groups from the reconciled hit `min`, with an explicit per-group lookup/consumption contract.** A sliding-window group is *hit-inert* when (a) it is EAGLE-annotated (`KVCacheGroupSpec.is_eagle_group`), so its hit length is not needed to bound the target's; (b) its window is shorter than `_cache_hit_alignment_tokens`, so its cached tail is only ever consultable at an alignment boundary; and (c) sparse retention is actually reachable for it: `need < alignment_tokens // block_size` (otherwise `reachable_block_mask` returns dense anyway, `single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:1027-1053`), `block_size` divides the alignment, and `extra_retained_tokens == 0` (it separately affects admission/retention sizing, `vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py:694-730` / `single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:888-895`; nonzero values require separate handling or exclusion).

   The group is still looked up. If its own hit reaches the candidate boundary, its blocks are consumed as today — that is how the retained boundary tail keeps a conversation's own follow-up turn warm. If its hit is *shorter*, it must neither shorten `curr_hit_length` nor inflate `longest_hit_length`, and its per-group result must be an explicit "no reusable blocks; allocate a fresh window", not the empty list the current lookup would return: today `find_longest_cache_hit` initialises empty per-group results (`kv_cache_coordinator.py:795-800`), fills them only for `attention_groups` (`:815-874`), and `KVCacheManager.get_computed_blocks` passes them straight to allocation (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_manager.py:228-294`), so an empty draft result cannot reuse a retained tail. This is the same per-group-boundary concern #53786 raises for SWA fine-grained hits, and it is the part that needs design agreement.

   **Unproven risk, stated plainly:** final outputs are protected by target verification, but the drafter's *acceptance* depends on the window's KV being valid. Whether a newly allocated window block is zeroed depends on `needs_kv_cache_zeroing` (`single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:88-94`); the design must guarantee the window is recomputed during prefill of the uncached remainder rather than read stale, and the acceptance dip while it refills has only been measured on the fork (decode-rate control within noise), not upstream. It is free whenever the remainder is at least one window — the diverging-prefix / new-turn case. #50457 (all-sliding DFlash drafter with prefix caching, PR) is in this area and may be the right home.

2. **Resolve the retention interval per KV cache group.** `KVCacheCoordinator` gains `retention_interval_by_group: tuple[int | None, ...]`, resolved once in `__init__` and indexed at both `cache_blocks` sites. The manager API is untouched (already per call). With the identity resolution behaviour is byte-identical, which the accompanying tests pin. The seam patch is ready and rebased on `22df3a3` — `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py` +37/−4, tests +72: https://github.com/nood-co1/vllm/tree/feat/per-group-prefix-cache-retention (commit https://github.com/nood-co1/vllm/commit/b9f82ae0f946039be1e96084ef15399e8cf2e07c). It is deliberately *not* opened as a PR: on its own it is plumbing with no user-visible effect, and it is only safe to use once part 1 exists.

3. **Policy:** resolve `retention_interval = 0` for groups that satisfy part 1's predicate, i.e. cache only the reachable-boundary tails (`SlidingWindowManager.reachable_block_mask`, `retention_interval == 0` branch), and the configured value for every other group. A genuine SWA target model (window spanning the alignment, or a group still inside the `min`) is unchanged. A user override can come later if wanted; the default should not need one.

Offered as a follow-up PR (parts 1–3 together, or 2 first if maintainers prefer the decomposition) once the policy is agreed.

### Feedback Period.

One week.

### CC List.

@rchalamala (#50457), @RichApple123 (#54397), @Suppressor72 (#53786 has the same DFlash2 all-sliding drafter shape), @woosebastian (#48532, eviction order in the shared pool).

### Any Other Things.

**Related work, and why this is not a duplicate** (`gh pr list` / `gh issue list --state open --search` for "per-group retention", "retention interval", "sliding window prefix cache eviction", "EAGLE draft prefix cache", 2026-09-01; titles verified with `gh` the same day):

- Issue [#48435](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48435) — hybrid-SWA prefix caching collapses under multi-session round-robin on Gemma-4 (eager-freed SWA tails recycled tail-first). Same LRU mechanism seen from the other side: there the SWA group *is* the target's own attention, its tails are needed for the hit, and losing them zeroes the hit. This RFC targets the case where the SWA group is a drafter whose hit is not needed; the eviction-order remedy for #48435 is different and the two compose.
- PR [#50457](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50457) — all-sliding DFlash drafter with prefix caching (open). Part 1 belongs near it.
- PR [#54397](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54397) — fine-grained SWA hits (draft). Orthogonal (lookup granularity, not retention or eviction).
- PR [#51886](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51886) — retention interval for `OffloadingConnector`; PR [#52747](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52747) — docs for the existing flag; PRs [#53803](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53803), [#53479](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53479), [#53945](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53945) — which Mamba checkpoints are materialized. None make the coordinator's retention per group.
- Issues [#53670](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/53670), [#53786](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/53786) — EAGLE last-block drop and SWA fine-grained hits on Qwen3.8/3.5 hybrids with DFlash2 drafters; same deployment shape, different costs.
- PR [#48532](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48532) — per-group eviction order in deferred block free (same pool, different path).

**Caveats.** All measurements are deployment evidence from a fork on GLM-5.3-Flash, which is not yet in `main` (#53906); the block-id arithmetic uses code paths that exist unchanged on `main` (`SlidingWindowManager.reachable_block_mask`, `BlockPool.free_blocks`). The pool size (643 ids) is derived from the logged `GPU KV cache size` / `max_concurrency` figure rather than logged directly — filed separately as a small observability request. The ~195K-per-conversation projection is from the capacity model (`642 >= 2C − D`), which predicted every measured row's sign and order but ran ~25% optimistic at retention 7168; the 120K × 2 reproduction above is the measured point.

Submitted by nood-co1 on behalf of Blockbrain Labs (https://x.com/blockbrain_labs, GitHub org blockbrain-ai); drafted with AI assistance (Claude, with an independent adversarial review pass by OpenAI Codex folded in) and reviewed by the submitter, who checked every `file:line` against `22df3a3`.

items.title: [RFC]: Preemption victim-selection extension point (least-computed-first as the first built-in)
items.body:
### Motivation.

When the V1 scheduler has to preempt a request to free KV cache, it does so by recompute: `_preempt_request` in `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py` resets the victim's `num_computed_tokens` to zero, and those tokens are computed again when the request resumes. This means the choice of which running request to evict directly decides how much compute a preemption throws away.

Neither of the current policies takes that into account. FCFS evicts the last request that was admitted, using `self.running.pop()`. PRIORITY evicts `max(running, key=(priority, arrival_time))`. Both ignore how much work a request has already done, so the scheduler can evict a request that has already prefilled several thousand tokens in order to admit a tiny one, and all of that computed KV is discarded.

I measured how much this costs. I call it the recompute tax, defined as recomputed tokens divided by total token compute. The numbers are in the Evaluation section below. The short version is that under KV pressure the tax is large, reaching about 79 percent in a forced offline sweep and 10 to 23 percent in realistic online serving, and a victim-policy ablation shows that the victim choice by itself accounts for roughly half of it. That half is something we can recover today with a policy that only looks at current state.

### Proposed Change.

I want to line this up with the Extensible Scheduler Plugin Framework in #51608 rather than propose something beside it. That RFC defines the QueueSort, Filter, and Score extension points, and it says explicitly that preemption remains a separate decision, deferring a preemption extension point to its phase 5. This RFC proposes the concrete design for that deferred point.

There are two parts.

The first part is an interim built-in that is already implemented in PR #53723 (open). It adds a `preemption_victim` setting that is orthogonal to the existing `policy` setting, which controls admission order.

- `SchedulerConfig.preemption_victim: Literal["fcfs", "lcf"] = "fcfs"`, with a matching CLI flag `--preemption-victim`.
- The default `"fcfs"` leaves the current behavior exactly as it is.
- `"lcf"` evicts the running request with the least sunk compute. LCF and PRIORITY share a single remove-and-restore path that is covered by tests, and the FCFS fast path through `pop()` is left untouched.

The second part is the actual ask. I would like to promote victim selection to a pluggable extension point under #51608, which is what its phase 5 anticipates. The interface would follow the read-only-feature contract that #51608 sets out, where a plugin receives read-only features owned by the scheduler rather than the scheduler's internal mutable objects.

```python
def select_victim(view: RunningView) -> RequestID: ...
# RunningView exposes read-only per-request features:
#   request_id, num_computed_tokens, num_cached_tokens,
#   arrival_time, priority, num_scheduled_tokens
```

The built-in policies `fcfs` and `lcf` would be the first implementations. The enum is the interim surface, and the plugin interface is the durable one.

One detail matters for correctness. The obvious key, `num_computed_tokens`, over-counts the real cost. When prefix caching and chunked prefill are on, some of a victim's computed tokens can be recovered from the cache on resume and are never actually recomputed. The key that reflects the true recompute cost is the number of computed tokens that are not cacheable, which is `num_computed_tokens - num_cached_tokens`. This RFC proposes that refined key. The key in #53723 today is `num_computed_tokens`, which is a conservative first version, and I will update it.

Fairness needs attention too. Because LCF evicts the request with the least sunk compute, it tends to pick requests that were only just admitted, so under sustained pressure a request could be preempted again and again and never make progress. Admission order still comes from FCFS or PRIORITY, so fairness at intake is unchanged, but the victim side needs a guard. I propose a per-request counter of consecutive preemptions, and once a request has been preempted more than a threshold K, it is protected from being chosen again and the tie-break moves toward older requests with more sunk compute. K would be configurable, and the default would be set high enough that the guard rarely fires under normal load. Measuring the worst-case starvation bound is part of the validation plan.

Finally, I would like to expose two Prometheus counters, `vllm:wasted_recompute_tokens_total` for the tokens discarded by preemption and `vllm:preemptions_total` for the number of preemptions, so that operators can see both the tax and the fact that LCF trades a few more but much cheaper preemptions.

### Evaluation.

I ran these on the Qwen2.5 family (0.5B, 7B-Instruct, 14B, and 32B) with ShareGPT prompts on A100 GPUs. The 7B model runs on a single GPU, and 14B and 32B run with tensor parallelism. The offline runs force KV pressure through `num_gpu_blocks_override`, and the online runs use `vllm bench serve` with a sweep over arrival rate. Wasted recompute is logged inside `_preempt_request` before the reset.

| Setting | Regime | Recompute tax (baseline) | LCF effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| Offline 0.5B, 300 reqs, seed 12345 | KV = 2800 of 4200 blocks | 0 percent, no preemption | not applicable |
| Offline 0.5B | KV = 1600 | 32.2 percent | wasted tokens down 59 percent |
| Offline 0.5B | KV = 800 | 57.9 percent | down 40 percent |
| Offline 0.5B | KV = 400, forced worst case | 78.8 percent | down 43 percent, from 623,948 to 354,882 tokens; per-preemption waste falls from 415 to 261 |
| Online 7B, 800 prompts, heterogeneous (`--random-range-ratio 0.5`) | under KV pressure | 10 to 23 percent | total wasted down 24 to 30 percent, and 35 to 41 percent per preemption, with throughput and latency unchanged |
| Online 7B, fixed 512-token input | under KV pressure | 10 to 23 percent | aggregate waste is unchanged, but the tail improves: mean TTFT down 24 percent, p99 down 21 percent, and goodput 6.4 times higher at a 0.05x KV cap |
| Scale 14B and 32B with tensor parallel | under KV pressure | 15 to 22 percent | wasted down 20 to 29 percent |
| Victim design-space ablation | under KV pressure | not applicable | the ordering is LCF better than LIFO, better than Random, better than most-computed-first, and victim choice alone is about 51 percent of the tax |

A few honest caveats. The 79 percent offline figure is an upper bound under forced pressure and does not represent normal load. In the fixed-length online case LCF does not reduce aggregate waste but gives a clear tail and goodput win, while under heterogeneous load it reduces waste directly. I have not yet quantified run-to-run variance with confidence intervals, and that is on the validation list.

### Alternatives considered.

I considered keeping only FCFS and PRIORITY and doing nothing about the victim key, but that leaves about half the tax on the table under pressure. I considered a clairvoyant policy such as SRPT or Gittins that is aware of remaining output length, but that needs output-length prediction, so I am treating LCF as the non-clairvoyant baseline that ships today and leaving the question of whether a predictive victim belongs in scope open for discussion. I considered avoiding recompute entirely through KV offload or swap rather than changing the victim, but that is a heavier and orthogonal change, and V1 is recompute-only by design, so victim choice is the change that costs no new infrastructure and still composes with offload later. I also measured most-computed-first and random victims, and both are strictly worse, as the ablation row shows.

### Rollout and validation.

1. Land the interim enum built-in in #53723, default off, with FCFS unchanged.
2. Add the `wasted_recompute_tokens` and `preemptions_total` metrics.
3. Refine the victim key to computed-minus-cacheable and re-run the offline and online sweeps.
4. Add the fairness guard as a consecutive-preemption cap and measure the starvation bound.
5. Define and implement `select_victim(RunningView)` under the #51608 phase 5 extension point, and move `fcfs` and `lcf` onto it.
6. Gate on validation: p99 TTFT and TPOT together with preemption-count deltas and run-to-run variance, correctness parity so the FCFS path is unchanged, and coverage with prefix caching and chunked prefill both on and off.

### Feedback Period.

Two weeks.

### CC List.

@yewentao256 and @chaunceyjiang, who authored the scheduler plugin framework in #51608.

### Any Other Things.

The reference implementation is PR #53723, which is open. I have the full per-run logs and the victim design-space ablation and can link them if that is useful.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] I searched existing issues and RFCs, including #51608 for the scheduler plugin framework, #45558 and #45561 for the priority victim key, and #49675 for zero-progress preemption, and none of them defines a preemption victim extension point.

items.title: [RFC]: Selective Weight Reload for RL Training
items.body:
**Authors:** [@new-TonyWang](https://github.com/new-TonyWang), [@aoshen524](https://github.com/aoshen524)  
**Organization:** inferact.ai  
**Based on:** Source-code audit of 88 PWAL implementations, 181 `replace_parameter` call sites, and 13 online quantization implementations.

---

## Motivation

vLLM's current weight hot-reload for RL training uses **layerwise reload**: move all params to meta device → re-materialize → re-run the full PWAL pipeline → `copy_` back to the original address. This approach has three problems:

1. **Extra VRAM** — temporary parameters double memory usage during the update window
2. **Unnecessary kernel rebuilds** — full PWAL re-execution includes kernel reconstruction for backends that don't need it (e.g., DeepGemm TMA reshape, FlashInfer TRTLLM 3D→4D, Aiter BMM pre-compilation)
3. **Irreversible repacks** — some PWAL operations (Marlin INT4, MXFP4) use `resize_()` which changes `data_ptr()`, breaking CUDA graph captures

The current mechanism treats all quantization methods identically, re-running the entire PWAL pipeline even when the vast majority of parameters can be updated with a simple `copy_()`. Our audit shows that **~75 of 88 PWAL implementations are pure delegation or no-ops** — they don't need re-execution on weight update.

### Current Call Chain

```
GPUWorker._start_weight_update()                    [gpu_worker.py:1347]
  → engine.start_weight_update()
    → initialize_layerwise_reload(model)              [layerwise.py:84]

engine.receive_weights()
  → model.load_weights(weights)
    → online_process_loader → _layerwise_process      [layerwise.py:332]
      → materialize_layer → replay loads → PWAL → copy_ back

GPUWorker.finish_weight_update()                     [gpu_worker.py:1410]
  → engine.finish_weight_update()
    → [RDT only: drain_pending()]
    → finalize_layerwise_reload(model, model_config)  [layerwise.py:289]
```

All three checkpoint engines (NCCL, IPC, Sharded RDT) follow this flow. The Sparse NCCL engine's start/finish are no-ops. Additionally, `gpu_model_runner.reload_weights()` (file-based reload) also uses layerwise.

---

## Proposed Change

### 1. First Principles and Immutable Constraints

**Core constraints:**

1. **`data_ptr()` must never change** — CUDA graph is already captured and will not be re-captured. All writes must use `copy_()` or `resize_()`+`copy_()`; `replace_parameter` (which creates new tensors) is forbidden.
2. **Firmly reuse `model.load_weights()`** — never bypass AutoWeightsLoader. Name routing, TP sharding, and `stacked_params_mapping` for 530+ models are fully reused.
3. **Do not use layerwise** — no dependency on meta device restore / materialize / `kernel_tensors` / `online_process_loader`.
4. **Never consider hot-swap** — always drain → update → resume.

**Design decisions:**

- **Three extension points, all declared as module-level protocols.** Each is a zero-argument method on `nn.Module`, with a default implementation that forwards to `self.quant_method` when one is present. A module that has no `quant_method` — or whose `quant_method` describes something other than its weights — implements the method directly. §6 explains why this shape, rather than hanging the protocol off `quant_method` alone.
  - **A — `weight_loader`** (load phase, per-param). The existing loader, unchanged. Six-category dispatch (①②③ complete eagerly / ④⑤⑥ staged for finish). See [Per-Param Copy Classification](https://claude.ai/code/artifact/7b259870-9f5c-40e4-9dd0-2cb238148307).
  - **B — `refresh_derived_state()`** (finish phase, per-module). A new interface, not PWAL. Contract: **in-place, idempotent, incremental, no `resize_()`**. Transformation logic is extracted from PWAL into shared pure functions. Only ⑤⑥ modules implement it; all others inherit the no-op.
  - **C — `restore_weights_before_loading()`** (start phase, per-module). Category ⑤ modules return params from runtime layout to checkpoint layout — transpose back, `resize_()` back to the original shape — so `weight_loader` works unmodified. Default is no-op. SGLang's wNa16 already ships this interface with zero callers. (Per-quant-method restore strategies: [SGLang Weight Update Landscape](https://claude.ai/code/artifact/a96c339c-7c1d-458a-9ad9-7a1f554b1576))
- **Enablement is per model, not per module.** A model uses the selective path only when every module in it is recognized and supported; otherwise the whole model falls back to layerwise. §10.
- **Fail-closed, twice over.** A dtype mismatch with no online quantization loader raises. A module type the enablement scan does not recognize disqualifies the whole model.
- **A failed update is terminal for the engine.** No in-engine rollback, no transaction. §11.

### 2. Quantization Landscape Audit

**Quantization granularity and buffer requirements:**

| Granularity | Scale Scope | Single Shard Independently Quantizable? | Representatives |
|------------|-------------|----------------------------------------|-----------------|
| Per-block (128×128) | Within 128×128 elements | **YES** — block falls entirely within single shard | Block FP8, MXFP4, MXFP8 |
| Per-group (128) | 128 contiguous elements | **YES** | GPTQ, AWQ (group_size=128) |
| Per-channel | 1 row/column | **YES** | INT8 SmoothQuant |
| Per-tensor | Entire tensor | **DEPENDS** — non-fused: yes; fused (qkv/w13): needs pairing | FP8 per-tensor |

> **Key finding:** The only case requiring a staging buffer is per-tensor scale × fused param × online quantization. All three conditions must be true. Block FP8 / per-group / per-channel have no such issue.

**vLLM quantization system scale:**
- **88** `process_weights_after_loading` implementations
- **181** `replace_parameter` call sites
- **13** online quantization PWALs (`online/` directory)
- **2** noop PWALs (embedding + moe_base)

### 3. What RL Training Frameworks Send

| Framework | Send dtype | Pre-quantized? |
|-----------|-----------|---------------|
| **veRL** | BF16 | No |
| **OpenRLHF** | BF16 | No |
| **Miles** | BF16 or FP8 | **Optional**: FP8 quantized on trainer side |
| **NeMo-RL** | BF16 | No |

> All mainstream frameworks send BF16 by default. Miles is the only one supporting trainer-side pre-quantization. **The initial implementation supports dtype-matched updates (BF16↔BF16, FP8↔FP8), covering 95%+ of real-world scenarios.**

### 4. Proposed Call Stack Design

#### START Phase

**Step 0** — `NCCLEngine.start_weight_update()`
> → drain requests

**Extension Point C** — `restore_weights_before_loading()`
> Walk the model in phase order (§6). For each module that implements it, call `module.restore_weights_before_loading()`.
> Category ⑤ modules perform their own inverse operation (transpose back / `resize_()` back to the original shape). Every other module inherits the no-op.
> **Purpose:** return params to checkpoint layout so `weight_loader` works correctly.

> **Why restore is needed — `weight_loader` only understands checkpoint layout:** `weight_loader` is configured at `create_weights` time (`output_dim=0, input_dim=1`), and it **always computes TP shard offsets and `copy_` positions using checkpoint layout rules**. It has no knowledge of post-PWAL transformations and no mechanism to update its own markers. For example, FP8 per-tensor dense PWAL transposes `[N, K]` → `[K, N]`, but `output_dim` remains 0 — during update, the trainer sends `[N, K]` tensors, `weight_loader` shards along dim=0 of the `[K, N]` param, and the shape mismatch causes an assertion failure. `restore` reverses the param back to the layout `weight_loader` understands; `weight_loader` needs zero modifications.

#### RECEIVE Phase

**Step 1** — `NCCLEngine.receive_weights(update_info)`
> → NCCL broadcast receives tensor

**Step 2** — `model.load_weights([(name, weight)])`
> → AutoWeightsLoader: checkpoint name → param routing (stacked_params / expert_params)
> → calls `param.weight_loader(param, loaded_weight, ...)`

**Extension Point A** — `weight_loader` (per-param)
> Already bound on the param at cold-start; directly reused during weight update. Dispatches into six categories based on the gap between arrival format and param format (①②③ complete eagerly / ④⑤⑥ staged for finish).
> See [Per-Param Copy Classification](https://claude.ai/code/artifact/7b259870-9f5c-40e4-9dd0-2cb238148307).

#### FINISH Phase

**Extension Point B** — `refresh_derived_state()`
> **What it does:** Walk the model in phase order (§6), calling `refresh_derived_state()` on every module that implements it. This is a **new interface**, not PWAL.
>
> **Three behaviours (fixed at cold-start; runtime is lookup-only):**
> - **Most modules** → `return`, do nothing. The copy phase already produced the final state. `NOOP`
> - **Format-transform modules** (category ⑤: Marlin / DEEPGEMM / FLASHINFER_TRTLLM / AITER) → Read the checkpoint-format data stored during the copy phase, call shared transformation pure functions to rearrange, `resize_()`+`copy_()` back to runtime layout. No kernel reconstruction. `REUSES PWAL TRANSFORM LOGIC`
> - **Derived state** (category ⑥) → Recompute secondary tensors from the updated source param, `copy_()` into pre-allocated positions. `DERIVE`
>   - W_UK_T / W_UV ← kv_b_proj (MLA projection matrices)
>   - _g1_alphas ← w1_scale × a1_scale (MoE fusion coefficients)
>   - mHC broadcast / HPC norm (DS4 broadcast copies)
>   - `_expert_map` / `expert_mask` ← parallel layout (EP routing tables; no checkpoint restores these)

> **Why a new interface instead of re-running PWAL:** PWAL's contract allows tensor reallocation, kernel reconstruction, and non-idempotent operations — all of which are bug sources during updates ([Weight Finalization Pipeline ch4](https://claude.ai/code/artifact/8044fcd7-01f8-477a-ba64-40206c8ddf42) has full evidence). `refresh_derived_state`'s contract from birth is **in-place, idempotent, incremental**. Transformation logic is extracted from PWAL into pure functions; the two entry points share computation code but use different write-back mechanisms (PWAL uses `replace_parameter`, refresh uses `copy_()`). Only modules that need finish-phase work implement it; the rest inherit the default no-op.

### 5. PWAL Classification and Derived State (Summary)

All 88 PWAL implementations classified by finish-phase behavior: **~40** pure delegation/noop (finish does nothing, eager `copy_` is final state), **~35** format transforms (update mode reuses transform code via `prefer_copy` / restore + `resize_()`+`copy_()`), **~5** derived-only + hook points ②③④ (refresh recomputes), **13** online quantization (migrated into `weight_loader` wrappers). Full census table and derived state inventory (W_UK_T/W_UV, W_K, W_UK_T_dcp_qrep, _g1_alphas, HPC norm, mHC broadcast) in [Weight Finalization Pipeline §4.5](https://claude.ai/code/artifact/8044fcd7-01f8-477a-ba64-40206c8ddf42).

> **Two hard conclusions that shape the design:**
> 1. Format transforms operate on the entire fused tensor (`w13_weight` contains all experts) — all weights must arrive before processing. **Cannot be eager** — this is the fundamental reason the finish phase exists.
> 2. MLA derived state has 3 paths (BF16 / MXFP4 / FP8); refresh dispatches by backend, reusing `_derive_absorbed_attention`. The dependency chain has two levels (`W_UK_T_dcp_qrep` ← `W_UK_T`); refresh follows dependency order.

### 6. Where the Extension Points Attach

The natural place to hang B and C is `QuantizeMethodBase`, mirroring PWAL's main loop. That turns out to be insufficient, and PWAL itself is the evidence.

#### PWAL reaches modules through four dispatch sites

`model_loader/utils.py::process_weights_after_loading` — the real driver — dispatches four different ways, with three different signatures:

| # | Condition | Call | Actually covers |
|---|-----------|------|-----------------|
| 1 | `isinstance(quant_method, QuantizeMethodBase)` | `quant_method.process_weights_after_loading(module)` | Every Linear / FusedMoE / Embedding carrying a `quant_method` — **plus attention layers with FP8 KV cache**, since `BaseKVCacheMethod` subclasses `QuantizeMethodBase` and `attention.py:211` assigns `layer.quant_method` |
| 2 | `isinstance(layer, (AttentionLayerBase, MMEncoderAttention))` | `module.process_weights_after_loading(model_config.dtype)` | `attention.py`, `mla_attention.py`, `mm_encoder_attention.py` |
| 3 | `isinstance(module, HpcModule)` | `module.process_weights_after_loading(model)` | Exactly one class: `HpcRopeNorm` |
| 4 | `hasattr(model, "process_weights_after_loading")` | `model.process_weights_after_loading()` | 7 implementations, all under `vllm/models/`: DeepSeek-V4 ×4 (nvidia model/mtp/dspark, amd model), dots3_note ×3 |

Site 1's loop body also calls `module.update_param_tp_status()` (2 implementers: `linear.py:291`, `vocab_parallel_embedding.py:336`). A fifth carrier exists one level down — `BasevLLMParameter.process_weights_after_loading()` at `parameter.py:517`, invoked from inside quant methods rather than by the driver.

Site 2 carries a standing upstream TODO:

```python
# TODO(lucas): see if there is a way to unify the signatures
# of process_weights_after_loading
```

#### Two consequences for this design

**Attaching only to `quant_method` leaves modules unreachable.** `HpcRopeNorm` — the target of PR E — is declared `class HpcRopeNorm(CustomOp, HpcModule)` and has no `quant_method` at all. Its derived state (`qnorm_weight` / `knorm_weight`, float32 copies pre-allocated as Parameters precisely so refit preserves captured addresses) is derived from *other* modules' weights via `self.fallback_qnorm` / `self.fallback_knorm`. A `quant_method`-only protocol cannot see it. The same holds for `RoutedExperts`' five `persistent=False` buffers (`_expert_map`, `expert_mask`, and three routing tables), which are derived from the parallel layout and restored by no checkpoint.

**Ordering is a hard dependency, not an artifact.** Site 2 runs strictly after site 1, and says why:

```python
# Initialize post-load attention weights for any attention layer and MM
# encoder. NOTE: Happens after other modules so we can easily decompress
# weights.
```

`model.modules()` yields in tree order, which interleaves attention layers among linear layers rather than placing them after. A single flat pass would therefore break this ordering. Site 4 is likewise deliberately last.

#### The resulting shape: one name, one signature, phased passes

`refresh_derived_state` and `restore_weights_before_loading` are declared on `nn.Module`, take no arguments, and default to forwarding to `self.quant_method` when one is present. Modules needing `dtype` or a reference to sibling modules capture them at `__init__`, which is what `HpcRopeNorm` already does. Ordering is preserved by making the passes explicit rather than implicit in the call-site sequence:

```python
for phase in (Phase.QUANT, Phase.ATTENTION, Phase.MODEL):
    for module in model.modules():
        if module_phase(module) is phase:
            module.refresh_derived_state()
```

This delivers what `TODO(lucas)` asks for — a single signature — without pretending the ordering constraint does not exist. PWAL itself is left alone: 88 implementations and a decade of accumulated call sites make unifying it a separate, much larger project. The two coexist, PWAL owning cold start and refresh owning reload.

A module reached by more than one PWAL site collapses to one `refresh_derived_state` that must do both jobs in order — an FP8-KV-cache attention layer refreshes its k/v scales before deriving `W_UK_T`.

### 7. Online Quantization Path Analysis

**Limitations of the current mechanism:**

vLLM's existing online quantization (`vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/online/`) has **all quantization logic in PWAL, not in `weight_loader`**. Cold-start flow:

```
create_weights  → BF16 param (no wrapping)
load_weights    → weight_loader unchanged, BF16 copy_ into BF16 param
PWAL            → BF16 → FP8/NVFP4/INT8 (replace_parameter)
```

After PWAL, the param becomes FP8. During weight update, the trainer sends BF16 → `copy_()` into FP8 param → dtype mismatch → failure.

**Existing `weight_loader` wrappers (none are online quantization):**

| Wrapper | Location | What it does | Online quant? |
|---------|----------|-------------|---------------|
| `MoeWNA16Method.get_weight_loader` | `moe_wna16.py:520` | AWQ/GPTQ INT4 bit repack | No, format transform |
| `Mxfp4MoEMethod.get_scale_weight_loader` | `mxfp4.py:623` | MXFP4 scale routing | No, scale routing |
| `make_online_process_loader` | `layerwise.py:146` | buffer → materialize → PWAL | Yes, but heavyweight layerwise |

**Solution: Lightweight `weight_loader` wrapper**

Permanently wrap `weight_loader` at `create_weights` time with inline quantization logic:

```python
def fp8_block_online_loader(param, loaded_weight, **kwargs):
    if loaded_weight.dtype == param.dtype:
        original_loader(param, loaded_weight, **kwargs)  # FP8→FP8
    else:
        fp8_data, scale = per_block_cast_to_fp8(loaded_weight)  # BF16→FP8
        original_loader(param, fp8_data, **kwargs)
        copy_scale(param, scale, **kwargs)
```

> **Block FP8 online quantization requires zero buffer:** each shard quantizes independently on arrival (block scale is local). Cold-start and weight update share one loader. No PWAL, no layerwise, no buffer.
>
> **Per-tensor FP8 online quantization requires a buffer:** fused params (qkv_proj, w13_weight) with per-tensor scale need all shards to arrive before computing `absmax`. Per-tensor FP8 is increasingly rare (mainstream is block FP8); can be deferred or use SGLang's w1+w3 closure buffer pattern.

### 8. Edge Cases: Per-Model Analysis

**DeepSeek-V3 / R1 (MLA + FP8 MoE)**

| Component | Weight Update Behavior | Required |
|-----------|----------------------|----------|
| Attention kv_b_proj | `copy_()` into kv_b_proj param | Finish: refresh W_UK_T / W_UV |
| Attention q/o proj | `copy_()` | None |
| MoE w13/w2 (block FP8) | `copy_()` (checkpoint layout = runtime layout for block FP8) | None |
| MoE w13/w2 (per-tensor FP8) | `copy_()` + finish: kernel shuffle via PWAL | restore → copy_ → PWAL (w1+w3 scale requantize + kernel shuffle) |
| `_g1_alphas` (per-tensor path) | — | Finish: refresh |

> **Block FP8 vs Per-tensor FP8:** Block FP8 PWAL does not transpose weights (`fp8.py:400`), does not call `process_fp8_weight_tensor_strategy`. So block FP8 MoE checkpoint layout = runtime layout — **direct `copy_()` works**. Per-tensor FP8 requires transpose + scale requantize + kernel shuffle and must go through PWAL.

**DeepSeek-V4-Pro (MLA + FP4 MoE, per-expert independent storage)**
- Experts stored independently (`experts.{i}.w1/w2/w3`), **no fused w13**
- Each expert is an independent tensor; online quantization can be done eagerly per-tensor
- No w1+w3 pairing issue
- MLA derived state same as V3
- **Uses the model-level PWAL hook** (dispatch site 4 in §6) — four of that site's seven implementations are DeepSeek-V4 variants, so the enablement scan of §10 must recognize it explicitly

**Kimi K3 (MLA + Latent MoE)**
- MLA derived state same as V3 (shared `_derive_absorbed_attention`)
- Latent MoE may have additional prefill/decode derived weights
- If using sleep mode (MNNVL fabric), KV state needs re-synchronization after weight update

**Llama / Qwen (Dense FFN, BF16)**
- Simplest case: all weights `copy_()`, no PWAL, no derived state
- Fused `gate_up_proj` and `qkv_proj` auto-routed via `stacked_params_mapping`

**Mixtral / Qwen3-MoE (FP8 MoE, fused w13)**
- fused `w13_weight` format
- Block FP8: direct `copy_()`
- Per-tensor FP8: needs PWAL (same as V3)
- INT4/Marlin: needs restore → copy_ → PWAL repack (shape change)

**Mamba / Jamba (State-space models)**
- Mamba has custom `weight_loader` (`mamba_mixer2.py:434`)
- conv1d weights have special sharding
- Mamba models are extremely rare in RL scenarios; can be deferred

### 9. Six-Category Full Coverage

All six categories are handled within the same C-A-B framework, enabled incrementally by PR. Per [Per-Param Copy Classification](https://claude.ai/code/artifact/7b259870-9f5c-40e4-9dd0-2cb238148307):

| Cat | Scenario | C (restore) | A (weight_loader) | B (refresh) | PR |
|-----|----------|-------------|-------------------|-------------|-----|
| **①** | BF16 dense/MoE, Block FP8 + Triton/CUTLASS | — | `copy_()` | return | PR A / PR B |
| **②** | dtype auto cast (BF16→FP16) | — | `copy_()` (auto cast) | return | PR A |
| **③** | Self-contained online quant (block FP8 / MXFP4 / MXFP8 / INT8) | — | Wrapped loader: per-block/channel quantize + `copy_()` | return | PR H |
| **④** | Cross-param online quant (per-tensor FP8 on fused / NVFP4 w1+w3) | — | Wrapped loader: per-expert eager buffer | return | PR I |
| **⑤** | FP8 per-tensor transpose | Transpose back to [N,K] | `copy_()` | Transpose back to [K,N] + requant | PR D |
| **⑤** | Block FP8 + DEEPGEMM/FLASHINFER/AITER | Restore layout | `copy_()` | Re-transform to runtime layout | PR D-moe |
| **⑤** | INT4/Marlin repack, MXFP4 repack | `resize_` back to original shape | `copy_()` | Repack | PR D-marlin |
| **⑥** | MLA derived state (W_UK_T / W_UV) | — | `copy_()` kv_b_proj | Recompute W_UK_T / W_UV | PR C |
| **⑥** | MoE Expert derived state (_g1_alphas, etc.) | — | `copy_()` scale | Recompute derived | PR F |
| **⑥** | HPC RopeNorm float32 copy | — | `copy_()` norm weight | Re-copy float32 | PR E |
| **⑥** | EP expert maps / routing tables | — | — (not transported) | Rebuild from parallel layout | PR F |

> **③④ are zero-invasive to ①②⑤⑥:** ③④'s wrapped loaders are bound to params at `create_weights` time. When `model.load_weights` calls `param.weight_loader`, the wrapped logic executes automatically. The three extension points (C/A/B) need no modifications.

### 10. Enablement and Fallback

Selective reload is enabled **per model**. A single scan at the start of an update answers one question — *is every module in this model recognized and supported?* — and the answer selects one path for the entire update.

```python
def use_selective_reload(model) -> bool:
    if envs.VLLM_FORCE_LAYERWISE_RELOAD:
        return False
    return all(module_is_supported(m) for m in model.modules())

# start_weight_update
if use_selective_reload(model):
    selective_start(model)          # C, phased passes
else:
    initialize_layerwise_reload(model)

# finish_weight_update
if selective_in_effect:
    selective_finish(model)         # B, phased passes
else:
    finalize_layerwise_reload(model, model_config)
```

`module_is_supported` is a **conservative whitelist**: a module qualifies when its type is known to the scan *and* its quantization method reports support. An unrecognized module type disqualifies the whole model. This makes the default fail-closed — new module types land on the layerwise path until someone deliberately adds them.

**Why per model rather than per module.** An earlier draft made this decision per module, so a model could run selective reload on its supported layers and layerwise on the rest. Whole-model enablement is preferred for four reasons:

- **No mixed intermediate state.** Under per-module dispatch, one update leaves some modules restored to checkpoint layout with live params, and others on meta device with buffered loads — two unrelated intermediate representations coexisting in one model. Whole-model enablement has exactly one.
- **The failure story is told once.** §11 describes what a failed update leaves behind. Under per-module dispatch that description has to cover both mechanisms and their interleaving.
- **No path conflict on shared modules.** Speculative-decoding proposers may assign the target model's module directly into the drafter (`spec_decode/gemma4.py:187`: `self.model.model.embed_tokens = target_embed_tokens`). One path restoring that module while the other moves it to meta device is a hazard that whole-model enablement removes by construction.
- **The test surface collapses.** Per-module dispatch has to be tested across combinations of supported and unsupported modules within one model; whole-model enablement has two paths, each tested once.

**The cost, stated plainly.** A model benefits only once *every* module type it contains is covered. DeepSeek-V3 needs PR B (block FP8), PR C (MLA refresh) and PR F (expert derived state) all merged before it switches; until then it stays on layerwise and gains nothing. PR B/C/F should therefore ship as a group. The tradeoff is accepted because "DeepSeek-V3 is supported as of vLLM x.y" is a clearer contract for downstream frameworks than a model that is partially converted.

**Known must-fallback methods.** These quantization methods and backends report no support, and therefore disqualify any model containing them:

| Method/Backend | Reason |
|---------------|--------|
| B12x Experts | `_release_source_parameters` releases original weight tensors, restore impossible |
| Destructive scale fusion MoE backends | `w13_weight_scale_2.mul_(input_scale)` is irreversible, refresh would double-fuse |
| Marlin-family repack (GPTQ/AWQ/FBGEMM/INT4) | `resize_()` changes `data_ptr()`, breaks CUDA graph |
| MXFP4 repack (Marlin path) | Same as above |
| AMX BMM path (MLA CPU) | Releases `kv_b_proj.weight` after processing |
| DeepGemm kernel (FP8 block) | Reshapes weights into TMA layout |
| Humming kernel (FP8 block) | Repacks into proprietary format |

`VLLM_FORCE_LAYERWISE_RELOAD=1` forces the legacy path unconditionally, as an operational escape hatch.

### 11. Failure Semantics

**A weight update that fails is terminal for that engine.** The exception propagates to the caller; the engine's weights are left in an undefined state; recovery is restarting the engine process. There is no in-engine rollback, no dirty-flag transaction, and no partial-retry path.

This is a deliberate choice, not an omission, and it matches what the ecosystem already does. Miles raises and lets orchestration handle it — `_make_request` annotates the `HTTPError` and re-raises, the update path contains no `try`/`except` at all, and `train/group.py` retries against a different cell ("cells w/ exceptions are auto marked errored, thus retry will find the next one") with `recover_updatable_engines` documented as "Restart any dead rollout engines." veRL is stricter still: its delta engine sets `_update_failed` on any exception, because "an earlier flush may already have changed runtime weights, so a later update would start from an unknown partial state," and refuses all subsequent updates with an instruction to restart the whole job.

The reason a softer guarantee is not offered: once `weight_loader` begins writing into live params, the previous weights are gone. Preserving them through the load phase means keeping a full shadow copy — which is precisely the layerwise memory cost this proposal removes. Rolling back is therefore unavailable by construction, and the honest contract is to say so.

Two obligations follow for implementations:

- Restore and refresh must **raise rather than silently continue**. A module that cannot restore its layout must not fall through to `weight_loader` with a runtime-layout param.
- Exceptions must carry **which module and which phase** failed, so the caller can distinguish a retriable transport fault from a defect in a specific quantization method.

Callers should treat a failed update as a signal to restart the rollout engine rather than to retry in place. In veRL's colocated mode this is inexpensive: the engine is asleep during the update window and serves nothing until the update completes, so a failure costs a sync round rather than corrupted rollouts.

### 12. Implementation Roadmap

Audited through two independent rounds (correctness audit + architecture/risk audit).

#### PR Sequence

**PR A: Selective Reload Core + Unquantized Enablement ①②** — Declare `restore_weights_before_loading()` / `refresh_derived_state()` on `nn.Module` with quant-method-forwarding defaults, plus `supports_selective_reload()` on `QuantizeMethodBase` (default False). New `selective.py` holding the whole-model enablement scan and the phased passes of §6. Three engines' start/finish choose a path once per update. `UnquantizedLinearMethod` / `UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod` / `UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod` report support. Includes the §11 failure contract and the module-type whitelist. **Verification:** BF16 small model end-to-end, `data_ptr` stability, layerwise regression, and a scan test asserting an unknown module type forces fallback.

**PR B-iface: Attention Refresh Implementation** (parallel with PR A) — `Attention`, `MLAAttention` and `MMEncoderAttention` implement the two module-level methods as no-ops and register in the `ATTENTION` phase. Under the §6 design these are ordinary implementers rather than a special dispatch site.

**PR B: Block FP8 Enablement ①** — Block FP8 on safe backends (Triton/CUTLASS/BlockWiseTorch), excluding DeepGemm and Humming kernels.

**PR C: MLA W_UK_T / W_UV Refresh ⑥** — 4 paths (BF16 / Aiter MXFP4 / Aiter FP8 / AMX CPU). W_UK_T_dcp_qrep two-level dependency chain. DCP all-gather coordination. FP8 path must not re-trigger Triton pre-compilation.

**PR D: FP8 Per-Tensor Transpose Restore + Refresh ⑤** — restore (transpose back to [N,K]) + refresh (transpose back to [K,N] + scale requant). Extract `process_fp8_weight_tensor_strategy` from PWAL as shared pure function.

**PR D-moe: MoE Backend Shape-Changing Restore + Refresh ⑤** — DEEPGEMM/FLASHINFER/AITER backends.

**PR D-marlin: Marlin/MXFP4 Repack Restore + Refresh ⑤** — `resize_()` back to checkpoint shape (cf. SGLang `_original_shapes`), refresh repacks.

**PR E: HPC RopeNorm float32 Copy Refresh ⑥** — `HpcRopeNorm` implements the module-level protocol directly; it has no `quant_method`, which is the case §6 exists to cover.

**PR F: MoE Expert and EP Routing Derived State ⑥** — `FusedMoEExperts` implements the protocol so TRT-LLM FP8 MoE can recompute `_g1_alphas`. Also covers `RoutedExperts`' EP maps (`_expert_map`, `expert_mask`, routing tables), which derive from the parallel layout and are currently repaired out-of-tree by veRL on ROCm.

**PR G: Model-Level Hook + gpu_model_runner Integration** — Register the `MODEL` phase so the model-level hook used by DeepSeek-V4 and dots3 participates (§6 site 4). `gpu_model_runner.reload_weights()` uses the same enablement scan. Comprehensive regression.

**PR H: ③ Self-Contained Online Quantization** — weight_loader wrapper framework + Block FP8 / MXFP4 / MXFP8 / INT8.

**PR I: ④ Cross-Param Buffered Online Quantization** — Per-tensor FP8 fused param per-expert eager buffer. NVFP4 w1+w3 buffer.

#### Dependency Graph

```
PR A (core + ①②)  ──┬──→ PR B (① block FP8)            ──┐
                     ├──→ PR D (⑤ FP8 transpose)          │
PR B-iface (attn)  ──┼──→ PR C (⑥ MLA refresh)            │
                     ├──→ PR D-moe (⑤ MoE backend)        ├──→ PR G (model hook)
                     ├──→ PR D-marlin (⑤ Marlin repack)    │
                     ├──→ PR E (⑥ HPC RopeNorm)           │
                     ├──→ PR F (⑥ Expert + EP maps)      ──┘
                     ├──→ PR H (③ self-contained online quant)
                     └──→ PR I (④ cross-param online quant)

Ship PR B + PR C + PR F together: DeepSeek-V3 switches paths only when all three land.
```

#### Risk Ranking

| Rank | PR | Risk | Reason |
|------|-----|------|--------|
| 1 | PR A (engine integration) | Highest | RDT quant-thread complexity, silent corruption risk |
| 2 | PR D (FP8 transpose) | High | restore/refresh cycle most complex, transpose + requant |
| 3 | PR C (MLA refresh) | High | 4 paths, DCP all-gather distributed coordination, pre-compilation |
| 4 | PR D-marlin (Marlin repack) | Med-High | Irreversible repack, `resize_` address issue |
| 5 | PR B (block FP8) | Medium | Kernel backend condition must be precise |
| 6 | PR G (model-level hook) | Med-High | DeepSeek-V4 depends on it; scan must recognize it or DS4 never converts |

#### Verification Matrix

| Model | Quantization | Categories | Expected Path | Verification PR |
|-------|-------------|-----------|---------------|----------------|
| Llama BF16 | None | ①② | selective | PR A |
| Mixtral BF16 MoE | None | ① | selective | PR A |
| Model with one unknown module type | any | — | **layerwise** (scan rejects) | PR A |
| DeepSeek-V3 block FP8 | FP8 block | ①⑥ | selective | PR B + C + F |
| DeepSeek-V4 | FP4 MoE | ①⑥ | selective | PR G |
| Llama FP8 per-tensor | FP8 per-tensor | ⑤ | selective | PR D |
| INT4 Marlin | Marlin | ⑤ | layerwise (must-fallback) | PR D-marlin |
| BF16 → block FP8 online | online FP8 | ③ | selective | PR H |
| BF16 → per-tensor FP8 MoE | online FP8 pt | ④ | selective | PR I |

### 13. SGLang/Miles Convergence

Our design independently converges with SGLang/Miles's approach. Miles's production RL pipeline follows the same boundary: **checkpoint format is the interface** — transport and `copy_()` always use checkpoint format; kernel/runtime format generation always happens in finish (PWAL). (Full analysis: [SGLang Weight Update Landscape](https://claude.ai/code/artifact/a96c339c-7c1d-458a-9ad9-7a1f554b1576))

Key differences:
- **Miles reruns full PWAL unconditionally** — this works because Triton/Marlin PWAL is idempotent and re-entrant, and restore handles INT4. vLLM cannot afford this — DEEPGEMM/FLASHINFER/TRTLLM backends have real overhead and reconstruct kernel objects.
- **Our `refresh_derived_state`** = Miles's boundary + contractualized selective increment (no-op modules return, in-place preserves `data_ptr`, kernel built only once).
- **Failure handling is deliberately identical** (§11): raise and let the caller restart.

SGLang's DeepSeek-derived `post_load_weights` already has informal versions of our three contracts: `bind_or_assign` (in-place), `weight_names` filtering (incremental), and `inverse_transform_scale_ue8m0` (non-idempotent workaround — evidence that without an "input must be checkpoint format" contract, you end up patching inverse transforms into derive).

The same convergence appears downstream in veRL, which reimplements C and B out-of-tree as a five-way `prepare`/`process` conditional — `prepare_quanted_weights_for_loading` is documented as "restore quantized params to the layout their `weight_loader` expects," and `stage_fp8_params_for_loading` as guaranteeing "no storage the CUDA graph captured is reallocated." A per-file account of what this proposal lets veRL delete is in [veRL Deletion Ledger](https://claude.ai/code/artifact/02ff3aa7-400b-43dd-a62f-b0b33e745158).

---

## Feedback Period

Two weeks from posting.

## CC List

@youkaichao @WoosukKwon @simon-mo @robertgshaw2-redhat

## Any Other Things

- This RFC supersedes the implementation approach in [#48312](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48312) (Weight Reload Correctness). #48312 remains the canonical failure taxonomy reference.
- Related merged PRs: [#49519](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49519) (Defer post-load attention weight processing), [#49558](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49558) (Filter packed expert weights during EP loading), [#51125](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51125) (Size w13 by shard count for non-gated MoE)
- Related open PRs: [#49459](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49459) (Reload layout-identical weights directly), [#52497](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52497) (Rank-local IPC weight updates)
- AI assistance was used in drafting this RFC. Both authors have reviewed and verified all technical claims against source code.

items.title: [RFC] Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: fp8_e4m3 KV cache on the QSA path — working patch, one machine, looking for corroboration
items.body:
## TL;DR

The QSA path of `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` refuses any KV dtype other than bf16. Most of
the machinery for fp8 is already in vLLM — only the **read** side of the QSA Triton
kernels was missing. Wiring it up roughly doubles the KV pool.

Measured on **one** GB10 (DGX Spark, sm_121):

| | bf16 | fp8_e4m3 | |
|---|---|---|---|
| KV pool | 780 638 tokens | **1 399 848** | ×1.79 |
| Max concurrency @ 262144 tok/req | 2.98× | **5.34×** | +79 % |
| Needle-in-a-haystack, 5 depths | — | **5/5** | |
| Decode, single stream, 100k ctx | — | 32.0 tok/s | no regression |

A working diff is here: https://gist.github.com/Nanetnounou/2e6486dd033bf077a9b8fdfcb6e1f7c8 (against vLLM `0.1.dev20073+g8e685d198`). **This is not a merge request yet** — see *What is not
tested* below. Posting it as an RFC because the interesting part may be the four
non-obvious integration points, and because a single machine is thin evidence.

## The problem

On a single 128 GB unified-memory box this model is attractive, but the KV pool
binds: at 262144 tokens per request the engine sustains ~3 concurrent requests, so
admission closes as soon as a queue forms — the normal regime under load, not an
incident.

`--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` fails with:

```
NotImplementedError: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next QSA requires a BF16 main KV cache
```

## What already worked

The change is small because most of it exists already:

| Piece | Before |
|---|---|
